title: Slow-cooker pork loin with apple and cider
subtitle: A gentle autumn pork braise with apple and dry cider
excerpt: Pork loin cooked with apple, onion, and dry cider until very tender. The cooking juices make a light, apple-scented sauce that is very good with the pork.
sourceNotes: Pork cooked with cider and apples is a tradition of West Country cooking in Britain, particularly in Somerset and Devon, where both pigs and orchards are abundant. The dish also appears in Normandy, France, under the name porc à la normande.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pork can rest in its cooking juices in the fridge for a day. Reheat gently in the slow cooker on LOW for 1 hour.

content.text: Pork loin is leaner than shoulder and cooks faster. Keep the cook time to 4 to 5 hours on LOW; beyond that the loin can begin to dry out. The apple and cider balance the mild flavour of the loin well.

The cooking liquid reduces to a thin but very flavourful sauce. For a thicker sauce, pour it into a small pan after the pork is done and reduce it over high heat for 5 minutes. A spoonful of cream stirred in at the end makes it richer.
Serve with roast potatoes, mashed potato, or braised red cabbage.

Season {{pork-loin}} of pork loin all over with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper-ground}} of black pepper. Place in the slow cooker. Arrange {{apple}} of apple quarters and {{onion}} sliced onion around the pork. Rub {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard over the top of the pork. Tuck in {{thyme}} of thyme and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Pour over {{dry-cider}} of dry cider and {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 4 to 5 hours. The pork is done when a probe thermometer reads 65°C at the thickest point, or when the juices run clear when you cut into it. Lift out carefully and rest on a board for 20 minutes. Discard the thyme and bay. Carve and serve with the cooking juices spooned over.

rows.symptom: The pork is dry after carving
rows.cause: Pork loin is very lean and dries out quickly if overcooked.
rows.fix: Slice it thinly and lay in the cooking juices before serving. Next time check at 4 hours and remove as soon as the temperature reads 65°C.

rows.symptom: The sauce tastes too sharp from the cider
rows.cause: Some dry ciders are quite acidic.
rows.fix: Stir in a teaspoon of honey and let it dissolve in the warm liquid. A splash of double cream also softens the acidity.

rows.cause: Apple breaks down very quickly in a moist heat environment.
rows.fix: Stir the dissolved apple through the sauce; it thickens and sweetens it. Add fresh sliced apple at serving time for texture.

rows.symptom: The cooking liquid is very thin
rows.cause: The cider and stock did not reduce during the low-heat cook.
rows.fix: Pour the liquid into a small pan and reduce over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes until it thickens slightly. Season and pour over the carved pork.

content.text: Pork with apple and cider is a classic of West Country cooking in Britain, rooted in a landscape where orchards and farmyards go together. The same pairing appears in Normandy, France, where cream is added to make porc à la normande. Both versions rely on the same principle: apple acidity sharpens the sweetness of pork and the cider carries those flavours into the sauce.
